team.name: healthhub-data
team.description: The people who keep HealthHub's data: its hospital catalogue, the medical conditions of the simulation, the admissions it records and the counts and series made from them. Ask them about any of HealthHub's tables, topics or pipelines.

domain.name: Healthcare
domain.description: Care delivery: the places care is given (hospitals, clinics, health stations), the conditions that bring people to them, their admissions and triage, and the activity counted from them. Source-aligned: the data as the systems that make it hold it.

dataProduct.name: HealthHub
dataProduct.description: HealthHub's data, end to end: the care centers of Catalonia, Brazil and Florida, a simulation of people falling ill and visiting hospitals, every admission with its triage at the desk by aityx, and the hourly admissions and patient days that datyx forecasts and scores. **The people are simulated, not real**: no row is about a real person, though the data is shaped and classified as if it were (PII and GDPR special category tags).

glossary.name: HealthHub
glossary.description: The terms of HealthHub's data: what a care center, an admission, a visit or a triage level means in its tables, topics and pipelines.

terms.name: Care Center
terms.description: A place where care is given: a hospital, a clinic or a health station (primary care), from public catalogues of Catalonia, Brazil and Florida.

terms.name: Hospital
terms.description: A care center of kind hospital: the only kind the simulation admits people to.

terms.name: Medical Condition
terms.description: A common illness the simulation gives people, with its treatment, how long it lasts and how it brings people to the hospital. Acute or chronic.

terms.name: Acute Condition
terms.description: A medical condition that passes: one course of visits, then the person is healthy again.

terms.name: Chronic Condition
terms.description: A medical condition that stays: courses of visits come back for as long as the simulation runs.

terms.name: Course
terms.description: The visits of one episode of a condition: a number of visits a number of days apart, the first, repeats and the last.

terms.name: Visit
terms.description: One trip to the hospital within a course: first, repeat or last. Each visit is an admission.

terms.name: Admission
terms.description: A simulated person's arrival at a hospital for a visit: who, what condition, which visit of the course, what they said, where and when (simulated day and minute). Recorded once per event id.

terms.name: Complaint
terms.description: What a patient says at the desk on arrival, filled from a template of their condition and visit; the only words, with their age, that triage reads.

terms.name: Triage
terms.description: How soon an arriving patient must be seen, where in the hospital they go and whether a nurse checks first, decided by aityx from their complaint and age, with the rule behind each answer.

terms.name: Triage Level
terms.description: The urgency of a triage, on five levels after the Manchester Triage System: red (immediate, 0 min), orange (very urgent, 10 min), yellow (urgent, 60 min), green (standard, 120 min), blue (non-urgent, 240 min).

terms.name: Simulated Person
terms.description: A synthetic person of the simulation, with a name, age, sex, job, home and conditions. Not a real person; their data is classified as a real person's would be.

terms.name: Run
terms.description: One start of the simulation, named by 8 hex digits: each replays the simulated calendar from day 1 with new people, so a person or a series is the run and its id together.

terms.name: Simulated Time
terms.description: The simulation's clock: day 1 is 2026-01-01, a real second a simulated hour by default. Days and hours in HealthHub's data are simulated, years ahead of the wall clock.

terms.name: Hourly Admissions
terms.description: The admissions at a hospital in a simulated hour of a run, in all and for acute and chronic conditions: the time series datyx forecasts with DeepAR. Sparse: an hour without admissions has no row, and means zero.

terms.name: Patient Day
terms.description: A simulated person's visits and hours of hospital care on a simulated day, with their facts: the series datyx scores with XGBoost for each patient's care in the next 30 days.

terms.name: Stay Hours
terms.description: The hours of hospital care a visit takes: its condition's stay for a first visit, its follow-up stay after.

terms.name: Move
terms.description: A simulated person's position and state each turn: at home, on the way to the hospital, there, or on the way back.

terms.name: Hourly Occupancy
terms.description: The people in care at a care center in a simulated hour of a run, each admission's stay counted in every hour it covers: the time series datyx forecasts with DeepAR for the care center view. Sparse: an hour nobody is in care has no row, and means zero.

termsOfUse: HealthHub's data is simulated: no row is about a real person, and none may be joined with real people's data. Use it to build and test analytics, forecasts and models; treat the columns tagged PII Sensitive and PersonalData SpecialCategory as if they were real (GDPR Art. 9), in access, retention and sharing.

database.description: HealthHub's PostgreSQL database: the care centers and medical conditions it is seeded with, the admissions its feed records from Kafka with their triage at the desk, the hourly admissions its Flink job counts, and the patient days view. HealthHub's API makes and describes the schema at every start. The people in it are simulated.

schemas.public: HealthHub's one schema: reference data (care_centers, medical_conditions, complaint_templates, greetings), events (admissions, admission_triage) and series (admissions_hourly, patient_days, occupancy_hourly).

checks.description: The feed has recorded admissions.
Every event id has the simulation's shape: run, person, day and turn.
No two admissions have the same event id: the feed records each event once, so a duplicate is an admission counted twice everywhere downstream.
Every person id is the person's city and number, such as sao-paulo-7: another shape is a person the simulation didn't make.
Every admission names its person: none is null or empty.
Every person is an adult of 18 to 90, the simulation's ages.
The people's ages spread over adulthood, their mean between 35 and 65 (about 48): a mean outside means the simulation's population is skewed.
Every person's sex is woman or man.
Every admission has the person's city: none is null or empty.
Every condition code has the seed's shape: lower case words joined by underscores.
Every condition is acute or chronic.
Every visit is the first, a repeat or the last of its course.
Visits are numbered from 1.
Some course starts at visit 1: the lowest visit number is 1, or courses are recorded without their first visit.
Every complaint is a sentence or a few, 20 to 1000 characters: a shorter or longer one is a template gone wrong, and triage reads it.
Every complaint has its placeholders filled: no brace is left of {name}, {age} and the others.
The complaint template is one of the visit kind's three, 0 to 2.
Every admission names its hospital: none is null or empty.
Simulated days count from 1.
Every arrival time is a minute of the day, HH:MM.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT id FROM admissions WHERE position(('-' || person_id || '-d' || sim_day || '-t') IN event_id) <> 9

checks.description: Every event id carries its own row's person and simulated day, after the run's id: a failure is an admission whose id and facts disagree, so which person or day it is can't be told.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT id FROM admissions WHERE (visit = 'first') <> (visit_number = 1)

checks.description: A first visit, and only a first visit, is visit number 1: a failure is a course whose visits are miscounted.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT split_part(event_id, '-', 1), person_id FROM admissions GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING count(DISTINCT age) > 1 OR count(DISTINCT sex) > 1 OR count(DISTINCT city) > 1

checks.description: Within a run, a person has one age, sex and city in all their admissions: a failure is two people mixed under one id, and patient_days would take either's facts.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT a.id FROM admissions a LEFT JOIN care_centers c ON c.id = a.hospital_id WHERE c.id IS NULL OR c.name <> a.hospital_name

checks.description: Every admission's hospital is a care center of care_centers, by id and under its name: a failure is an admission at a place the catalogue doesn't have, or has under another name.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT a.id FROM admissions a LEFT JOIN medical_conditions m ON m.code = a.condition_code WHERE m.code IS NULL OR m.name <> a.condition_name OR m.type <> a.condition_type

checks.description: Every admission's condition is in medical_conditions, with the same name and type: a failure is a condition the seed dropped or changed, whose stays patient_days and occupancy_hourly can't count.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT a.id FROM admissions a JOIN medical_conditions m ON m.code = a.condition_code WHERE a.age < m.min_age OR a.age > m.max_age

checks.description: Every person is within their condition's ages (min_age to max_age): the simulation picks conditions by age, so a failure is a condition given to someone it can't occur in.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT a.id FROM admissions a JOIN medical_conditions m ON m.code = a.condition_code WHERE m.type = 'acute' AND a.visit_number > m.visit_count

checks.description: An acute condition's visits are numbered up to its course's visit_count: a failure is a course that went on past its end.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT a.id FROM admissions a LEFT JOIN complaint_templates t ON t.condition_code = a.condition_code AND t.visit = a.visit AND t.position = a.template WHERE a.template IS NOT NULL AND t.id IS NULL

checks.description: Every admission's template is one of complaint_templates for its condition and visit: a failure is a complaint whose reference triage level can't be found.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT id FROM admissions WHERE recorded_at > now() + INTERVAL '5 minutes'

checks.description: No admission is recorded later than now: a failure is a clock gone wrong on the API's host.
Every event id has the simulation's shape: run, person, day and turn.
Every level is one of the five Manchester levels.
Every reference level is one of the five Manchester levels.
Every wait is its level's: 0, 10, 60, 120 or 240 minutes.
Every area is one of the hospital's six.
The level's rule is a row of the decision table, from 1.
The area's rule is a row of the decision table, from 1.

Every call ended within its timeouts: aityx's client gives connecting 10 s and sending and reading the answer 60 s each, so a call, answered or failed, takes about 130 s at most; the bound is 180 s. A failure is a call that outlived them (a client that hung) or a clock gone wrong. A slow aityx shows as times near the bound, and errors, not as a failure.
Token counts are never negative.
aityx ran each call in one of its modes: defined, jev or jev_aityx.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT t.event_id FROM admission_triage t LEFT JOIN admissions a ON a.event_id = t.event_id WHERE a.event_id IS NULL

checks.description: Every triage is of an admission in admissions: a failure is a triage of nobody, whose patient can't be found.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT event_id FROM admission_triage WHERE (level IS NULL) = (error IS NULL)

checks.description: A triage has a level or an error, never both nor neither: a failure is a triage that both failed and decided, or did neither.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT event_id FROM admission_triage WHERE level IS NOT NULL AND (wait_minutes IS NULL OR area IS NULL OR nurse_check IS NULL OR level_rule IS NULL OR area_rule IS NULL)

checks.description: A triage with a level has its wait, area, nurse's check and both rules: a failure is a decision recorded in part.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT event_id FROM admission_triage WHERE level IS NOT NULL AND wait_minutes IS DISTINCT FROM CASE level WHEN 'red' THEN 0 WHEN 'orange' THEN 10 WHEN 'yellow' THEN 60 WHEN 'green' THEN 120 WHEN 'blue' THEN 240 END

checks.description: Every wait is its own level's (red 0, orange 10, yellow 60, green 120, blue 240 minutes): a failure is a patient told to wait longer or shorter than their level allows.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT t.event_id FROM admission_triage t JOIN admissions a ON a.event_id = t.event_id LEFT JOIN complaint_templates c ON c.condition_code = a.condition_code AND c.visit = a.visit AND c.position = a.template WHERE t.reference IS DISTINCT FROM c.triage

checks.description: Every reference level is the triage level of the template the admission's complaint was said from (none without one): a failure makes aityx's agreement with the reference wrong.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT t.event_id FROM admission_triage t JOIN admissions a ON a.event_id = t.event_id WHERE t.triaged_at < a.recorded_at

checks.description: No admission is triaged before it is recorded: a failure is a clock or an order gone wrong.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT count(*) FROM admission_triage WHERE level IS NOT NULL AND reference IS NOT NULL AND level <> reference

checks.description: Information, never a failure: how many triages decided another level than the template's reference level, aityx's disagreements to look at (about 5% of triages).
The Flink job has counted admissions.
The table has its seven columns: datyx's DeepAR groups read it, and a column added or gone changes what they train on.
run_id is there: with hospital_id, the key of each series DeepAR forecasts.
hospital_id is there: with run_id, the key of each series DeepAR forecasts, and its static category.
hour_start is there: the timestamp of every DeepAR group of the table.
admissions is there: the default DeepAR group's target.
acute_admissions is there: the acute DeepAR group's target.
chronic_admissions is there: the chronic DeepAR group's target.
Every run id is 8 hex digits.
Every row names its hospital: none is null or empty.
Sparse: a row is an hour with at least one admission.
No hospital has more than 100 admissions in a simulated hour, more than any city's simulated people: a higher count is admissions counted twice.
Counts are never negative.
Counts are never negative.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT run_id, hospital_id, hour_start FROM admissions_hourly WHERE acute_admissions + chronic_admissions <> admissions

checks.description: Every hour's acute and chronic admissions add up to its admissions: a failure is a count the acute and chronic forecasts and the default one disagree on.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT run_id, hospital_id, hour_start FROM admissions_hourly WHERE hour_start <> date_trunc('hour', hour_start) OR hour_start < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'

checks.description: Every hour starts on the hour, on or after day 1 (2026-01-01): a failure is a step DeepAR's hourly series can't place.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT h.run_id, h.hospital_id, h.hour_start FROM admissions_hourly h LEFT JOIN care_centers c ON c.id = h.hospital_id WHERE c.id IS NULL OR c.name <> h.hospital_name

checks.description: Every row's hospital is a care center of care_centers, by id and under its name: a failure is a series of a place the catalogue doesn't have.

parameters.sqlExpression: WITH counted AS ( SELECT split_part(a.event_id, '-', 1) AS run_id, a.hospital_id, TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01' + (a.sim_day - 1) * INTERVAL '1 day' + split_part(a.sim_time, ':', 1)::int * INTERVAL '1 hour' AS hour_start, count(*) AS admissions, count(*) FILTER (WHERE a.condition_type = 'acute') AS acute, count(*) FILTER (WHERE a.condition_type = 'chronic') AS chronic FROM admissions a WHERE a.event_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-' AND a.sim_time ~ '^[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ), settled AS ( SELECT split_part(event_id, '-', 1) AS run_id, max(TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01' + (sim_day - 1) * INTERVAL '1 day' + split_part(sim_time, ':', 1)::int * INTERVAL '1 hour') AS hour FROM admissions WHERE event_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-' AND sim_time ~ '^[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]' AND recorded_at < now() - INTERVAL '2 minutes' GROUP BY 1 ) SELECT h.run_id, h.hospital_id, h.hour_start FROM admissions_hourly h JOIN settled s ON s.run_id = h.run_id AND h.hour_start < s.hour LEFT JOIN counted c ON c.run_id = h.run_id AND c.hospital_id = h.hospital_id AND c.hour_start = h.hour_start WHERE h.admissions > coalesce(c.admissions, 0) OR h.acute_admissions > coalesce(c.acute, 0) OR h.chronic_admissions > coalesce(c.chronic, 0)

checks.description: Flink counts no admission the admissions table hasn't: for every run with admissions, no settled hour (before the hour of the run's latest admission recorded two minutes ago or more, so the feed has caught up) has more admissions, acute or chronic ones in admissions_hourly than admissions holds, nor a row where it holds none. Both read the same topic; Flink's documented gaps (a restart recounting from the topic's start, an hour at the edge of its one-day retention rewritten lower, Flink holding counts back while the database is down) only ever count fewer, so a failure is admissions the API's feed lost from the topic. Runs without admissions (a generated history) aren't compared.

parameters.sqlExpression: WITH counted AS ( SELECT split_part(a.event_id, '-', 1) AS run_id, a.hospital_id, TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01' + (a.sim_day - 1) * INTERVAL '1 day' + split_part(a.sim_time, ':', 1)::int * INTERVAL '1 hour' AS hour_start, count(*) AS admissions FROM admissions a WHERE a.event_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-' AND a.sim_time ~ '^[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ), settled AS ( SELECT split_part(event_id, '-', 1) AS run_id, max(TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01' + (sim_day - 1) * INTERVAL '1 day' + split_part(sim_time, ':', 1)::int * INTERVAL '1 hour') AS hour FROM admissions WHERE event_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-' AND sim_time ~ '^[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]' AND recorded_at < now() - INTERVAL '2 minutes' GROUP BY 1 ) SELECT count(*) FROM counted c JOIN settled s ON s.run_id = c.run_id AND c.hour_start < s.hour LEFT JOIN admissions_hourly h ON h.run_id = c.run_id AND h.hospital_id = c.hospital_id AND h.hour_start = c.hour_start WHERE coalesce(h.admissions, 0) < c.admissions

checks.description: Information, never a failure: how many settled hours of runs with admissions Flink counted fewer admissions for than the admissions table holds, or not at all. HealthHub's own spec allows it: a restarted job recounts the topic from 1 up, an hour at the edge of the topic's one-day retention is rewritten with the part left, and a database that was down holds the counts back. Zero once Flink has caught up; a number that stays and grows is Flink falling behind.

The view has the columns of datyx's care group (XGBoost): run_id and person_id the series, day the timestamp, stay_hours the target, sex, city, hospital_id, chronic_condition and age the person's facts, visits, acute_visits and chronic_visits the past covariates. A change here is a change for the group's roles.
Every run id is 8 hex digits.
Sparse: a row is a day with at least one visit.
Every person is an adult of 18 to 90.
Every person's sex is woman or man.
Every row says its chronic condition, none spelled out: never null or empty.
Every day's visits have their hours of care: no visit is of a condition the seed no longer has.
A day's care is 1 to 144 hours: at most two visits of up to 72.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT run_id, person_id, day FROM patient_days GROUP BY run_id, person_id, day HAVING count(*) > 1

checks.description: One row per run, person and day: a duplicate is a day XGBoost would count twice.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT run_id, person_id, day FROM patient_days WHERE acute_visits + chronic_visits <> visits

checks.description: Every day's acute and chronic visits add up to its visits: a failure is a visit of a condition neither acute nor chronic.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT run_id, person_id, day FROM patient_days WHERE stay_hours < visits OR stay_hours > 72 * visits

checks.description: A day's hours of care are at least an hour a visit and at most 72 a visit, a stay's longest: a failure is a stay counted wrong for its visits.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT p.run_id, p.person_id, p.day FROM patient_days p WHERE p.chronic_condition <> 'none' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM medical_conditions m WHERE m.code = p.chronic_condition AND m.type = 'chronic')

checks.description: Every chronic condition named is a chronic condition of medical_conditions: a failure is a category XGBoost learns that the seed doesn't have.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT run_id, person_id, day FROM patient_days WHERE chronic_visits > 0 AND chronic_condition = 'none'

checks.description: A day with chronic visits names the person's chronic condition: a failure is a chronic visit of no chronic condition.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT p.run_id, p.person_id, p.day FROM patient_days p LEFT JOIN care_centers c ON c.id = p.hospital_id WHERE c.id IS NULL

checks.description: Every day's hospital is a care center of care_centers: a failure is a category of a place the catalogue doesn't have.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT run_id, person_id, day FROM patient_days WHERE day < DATE '2026-01-01'

checks.description: Every day is on or after day 1 of the simulation, 2026-01-01.
The view has its five columns: datyx's DeepAR group reads it, and a column added or gone changes what it trains on.
run_id is there: with hospital_id, the key of each series DeepAR forecasts.
hospital_id is there: with run_id, the key of each series DeepAR forecasts.
hour_start is there: the timestamp of the DeepAR group.
occupancy is there: the DeepAR group's target.
Every run id is 8 hex digits.
Sparse: a row is an hour with someone in care, never negative.
No care center has more than 100 people in care at once, more than any city's simulated people: a higher count is stays counted twice.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT run_id, hospital_id, hour_start FROM occupancy_hourly GROUP BY run_id, hospital_id, hour_start HAVING count(*) > 1

checks.description: One row per run, care center and hour: a duplicate is an hour DeepAR would read twice.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT run_id, hospital_id, hour_start FROM occupancy_hourly WHERE hour_start <> date_trunc('hour', hour_start) OR hour_start < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'

checks.description: Every hour starts on the hour, on or after day 1 (2026-01-01).

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT o.run_id, o.hospital_id, o.hour_start FROM occupancy_hourly o LEFT JOIN care_centers c ON c.id = o.hospital_id WHERE c.id IS NULL OR c.name <> o.hospital_name

checks.description: Every row's care center is one of care_centers, by id and under its name.

parameters.sqlExpression: WITH arrivals AS ( SELECT split_part(a.event_id, '-', 1) AS run_id, a.hospital_id, date_trunc('hour', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01' + (a.sim_day - 1) * INTERVAL '1 day' + a.sim_time::time) AS hour_start, count(DISTINCT a.person_id) AS people FROM admissions a JOIN medical_conditions m ON m.code = a.condition_code WHERE a.event_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ) SELECT r.run_id, r.hospital_id, r.hour_start FROM arrivals r LEFT JOIN occupancy_hourly o ON o.run_id = r.run_id AND o.hospital_id = r.hospital_id AND o.hour_start = r.hour_start WHERE o.occupancy IS NULL OR o.occupancy < r.people

checks.description: Everyone who arrives at a care center is in care there in the hour they arrive: an hour has at least as many people in care as arrived in it. A failure is a stay the view lost.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT o.run_id, o.hospital_id, o.hour_start FROM occupancy_hourly o JOIN (SELECT split_part(event_id, '-', 1) AS run_id, max(TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01' + (sim_day - 1) * INTERVAL '1 day' + sim_time::time) AS latest FROM admissions WHERE event_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-' GROUP BY 1) r ON r.run_id = o.run_id WHERE o.hour_start > date_trunc('hour', r.latest)

checks.description: No hour is after the run's latest arrival, its now: a failure is occupancy counted ahead of the simulation, a stay's hours to come.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT count(*) FROM occupancy_hourly o JOIN care_centers c ON c.id = o.hospital_id WHERE o.occupancy > CASE c.kind WHEN 'hospital' THEN 12 WHEN 'health_station' THEN 5 ELSE 6 END

checks.description: Information, never a failure: how many hours a care center had more people in care than the largest capacity of its kind in the simulation (12 beds at a hospital, 6 places at a clinic, 5 at a health station). The occupancy alarms are about such hours; a care center's own capacity, drawn from its key, is often smaller.
The seed is there.
No two care centers have the same key, the seed's own: a duplicate is a care center seeded twice.
Every care center has a name: none is null or empty.
Every care center is a hospital, a clinic or a health station.
Every care center has its city: none is null or empty.
Every care center is in Spain, Brazil or the United States.
Latitudes are on the globe.
Longitudes are on the globe.
Ownership is public, private or unknown.
Every postal code has its country's shape: five digits, or Brazil's five and three (01243-906).
Every website is a web address, a host name with a dot and an optional http(s) scheme and path: a failure is a link the app would open to nowhere.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT id FROM care_centers WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL AND key <> source || ':' || source_id

checks.description: A care center with a source id is keyed by its source and that id: a failure is a key that won't match the source's record at the next seed, so it would be seeded again.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT id FROM care_centers WHERE (latitude IS NULL) <> (longitude IS NULL) OR (latitude IS NOT NULL AND NOT CASE country WHEN 'ES' THEN latitude BETWEEN 27 AND 44 AND longitude BETWEEN -19 AND 5 WHEN 'BR' THEN latitude BETWEEN -34 AND 6 AND longitude BETWEEN -74 AND -34 WHEN 'US' THEN latitude BETWEEN 18 AND 72 AND longitude BETWEEN -180 AND -65 ELSE false END)

checks.description: Every care center with a position has both coordinates, within its country: a failure is a latitude and longitude swapped or a sign lost, a place drawn on the wrong continent.
The seed is there.
Every code is lower case words joined by underscores, as admissions carry it.
Every condition is acute or chronic.
Adult ages only.
Adult ages only.
Every condition has its summary, which HealthHub shows: none is empty.
Every condition has its treatment, which HealthHub shows: none is empty.
A treatment lasts a day or more.
A share, 0 to 1.
A first visit stays 1 to 72 hours.
A later visit stays 1 to 72 hours.
A course has at least one visit.
Visits are at least a day apart.
The gap between courses is never negative.
The first visit goes to one of the simulation's settings: hospital, primary, urgent_care, mental_health or dialysis.
The later visits go to one of the simulation's settings: hospital, primary, urgent_care, mental_health or dialysis.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT code FROM medical_conditions WHERE prevalence <= 0

checks.description: Every condition is drawn at times: its prevalence is above zero. A failure is a condition the simulation never gives.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT code FROM medical_conditions WHERE min_age > max_age

checks.description: Every condition's youngest age is at most its oldest: a failure is a condition nobody can have.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT code FROM medical_conditions WHERE (type = 'acute') <> (treatment_duration_days IS NOT NULL)

checks.description: An acute condition's treatment lasts so many days, a chronic one's has no end: a failure is a treatment length where it can't be, or missing where it must be.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT m.code FROM medical_conditions m LEFT JOIN complaint_templates t ON t.condition_code = m.code GROUP BY m.code HAVING count(t.id) <> 9 OR count(DISTINCT (t.visit, t.position)) <> 9

checks.description: Every condition has its nine complaint templates, three for each of its first, repeat and last visits: a failure is a visit the simulation can't put into words.
Every template is for a first, repeat or last visit.
Three templates per condition and visit, 0 to 2.
Every template is a sentence or a few, 20 to 1000 characters.
Every template has its reference triage level.
Every reference level is one of the five Manchester levels.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT condition_code, visit, position FROM complaint_templates GROUP BY condition_code, visit, position HAVING count(*) > 1

checks.description: One template per condition, visit and position: a duplicate makes which one an admission was said from ambiguous.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT t.id FROM complaint_templates t LEFT JOIN medical_conditions m ON m.code = t.condition_code WHERE m.code IS NULL

checks.description: Every template is of a condition in medical_conditions: a failure is a template no admission can use.

parameters.sqlExpression: SELECT id FROM complaint_templates WHERE regexp_replace(text, '[{](name|first_name|age|sex|occupation|city|hospital|visit_number|days_since_first_visit)[}]', '', 'g') ~ '[{}]'

checks.description: Every placeholder in a template is one the simulation fills ({name}, {first_name}, {age}, {sex}, {occupation}, {city}, {hospital}, {visit_number}, {days_since_first_visit}): a failure is a brace left in a patient's words.
One greeting, written at the first start.
The greeting is HealthHub's own, Hello, world.

healthhub.admissions.description: Every simulated arrival at a hospital, as HealthHub's simulation publishes it through Kafka's REST proxy, keyed by the person. HealthHub's API records each in the admissions table, and the Flink job counts them per hospital and hour. Kept 24 hours. The people are simulated.

fields.eventId: The event's id: the run, the person, the day and the turn, as <run>-<person>-d<day>-t<turn>; unique.
fields.personId: The simulated person's id within the run, such as reus-3.
fields.name: The simulated person's name.
fields.age: The person's age in years, 18 to 90.
fields.sex: The person's sex: woman or man.
fields.city: The city the person lives in.
fields.visit: Which visit of the course: first, repeat or last.
fields.visitNumber: The visit's number in the course, from 1.
fields.complaint: What the patient says on arrival.
fields.template: Which of the visit kind's complaint templates it was said from, 0 to 2.
fields.simTime: The simulated minute of arrival, HH:MM.
fields.day: The simulated day, from 1 at each run's start.
fields.turn: The simulation's turn, an hour of simulated time by default.

healthhub.admissions.hourly.description: The admissions per run, hospital and simulated hour, upserted by HealthHub's Flink job (admissions-hourly) as it counts healthhub.admissions; the same rows it writes to the admissions_hourly table. Keyed by run, hospital and hour, so the latest record of a key is its count.

fields.hour_start: The simulated hour, ISO 8601 without a time zone: day 1 is 2026-01-01.
fields.admissions: The admissions in the hour; acute and chronic add up to it.
fields.acute_admissions: The admissions in the hour for an acute condition.
fields.chronic_admissions: The admissions in the hour for a chronic condition.

healthhub.people.moves.description: Every simulated person's move, once a turn, as HealthHub's simulation publishes it, keyed by the person: where they are, where home and their hospital are, and what they are doing. HealthHub's map reads it back; it isn't stored. Kept 24 hours. The people are simulated.

fields.id: The simulated person's id within the run, such as reus-3.
fields.name: The simulated person's name.
fields.age: The person's age in years, 18 to 90.
fields.city: The city the person lives in.
fields.lat: Where the person is now: latitude, WGS84.
fields.lon: Where the person is now: longitude, WGS84.
fields.state: What the person is doing: home, to_hospital, at_hospital or to_home.
fields.mode: How the person travels, by the distance from home to the hospital: walk (up to 2 km), transit (up to 15 km) or car.
fields.monitored: Whether the person is monitored at home, the high-risk only: their moves at home are check-ins.
fields.monitoredFor: Why the person is monitored at home, such as "aged 84" or "pregnant"; null when they aren't.
fields.conditionName: The condition of the visit under way; at home, the acute episode's if one is on, else the chronic condition's; null while healthy.
fields.conditionType: That condition's type: acute or chronic; null while healthy.
fields.day: The simulated day, from 1 at each run's start.

healthhub.test.description: The topic of HealthHub's live Kafka test (healthhub_api/test/kafka_rest_live_test.dart): a record produced through the REST proxy and consumed back, apart from the simulation's topics so a test never writes into what a running API reads. Made by the kafka service's health check. No business data.

fields.id: The test run's id, live-<random>, also the record's key.

service.name: healthhub-api
service.description: HealthHub's API (Dart): it runs the simulation of people, records what it publishes, and triages each admission with aityx.

pipelines.name: simulation
pipelines.description: Simulated people living in the cities of the care centers: each falls ill with the seeded conditions, travels to their hospital for each visit of a course, and is admitted on arrival. Every turn it publishes each person's move to healthhub.people.moves, and each arrival to healthhub.admissions.

tasks.people: Makes the run's people, each with a home near a city's hospital, a job and conditions weighed by age and sex.
tasks.move: Each turn, moves every person a step and publishes the move.
tasks.admit: On arrival at the hospital, publishes the admission with a complaint from the condition's templates.

service.name: healthhub-api
service.description: HealthHub's API (Dart): it runs the simulation of people, records what it publishes, and triages each admission with aityx.

pipelines.name: admissions-feed
pipelines.description: Reads healthhub.admissions in a stable consumer group and records each valid admission in the admissions table, once per event id, so a replay never doubles one.

tasks.consume: Polls the topic through Kafka's REST proxy, from where it left off.
tasks.record: Inserts each admission, skipping an event id already there.

service.name: healthhub-api
service.description: HealthHub's API (Dart): it runs the simulation of people, records what it publishes, and triages each admission with aityx.

pipelines.name: triage
pipelines.description: Triages each admission it records with aityx, from the complaint and the age only: Jev reads the danger signs and choices, a decision (Manchester Triage System levels) gives the level, the wait, the area and a nurse's check. Writes admission_triage, with the template's reference level beside it.

tasks.ask: One call to aityx per admission, four at a time.
tasks.record: Keeps the triage, its rules and aityx's receipt, or why it failed.

service.name: healthhub-flink
service.description: HealthHub's Flink cluster (a JobManager and a TaskManager), running its streaming SQL jobs.

pipelines.name: admissions-hourly
pipelines.description: Flink SQL (HealthHub/flink/admissions-hourly.sql): reads healthhub.admissions from the earliest record, drops malformed and repeated events, counts the admissions per run, hospital and simulated hour, in all and acute and chronic, and upserts each count to the healthhub.admissions.hourly topic and the admissions_hourly table.

tasks.admission_events: The topic as a table: the admission's type, event id, hospital, condition type, day and minute.
tasks.admissions_once: Valid admissions only, each event id once, with the simulated hour it falls in.
tasks.hourly: The counts per run, hospital and hour.
tasks.sink: Upserts each count to the topic and the table by its key.

lineage.description: The simulation sends people to the hospitals among the care centers.
The conditions decide when people travel and how long they stay.
An admission names the hospital the person arrives at.
An admission names the condition that brings the person, and its visit of the course.
An admission's complaint is filled from one of its condition's templates.
The feed records each admission once.
aityx triages each recorded admission from its complaint and age.
The triage keeps the template's reference level beside aityx's.
The Flink job counts the admissions per run, hospital and hour.
The same counts, upserted to a topic.
The view groups each person's admissions by run and simulated day.
The view takes each visit's hours of care from its condition.
The view counts each admission's stay in every simulated hour it covers.
The view takes each stay's hours from its condition.
